discovered: The camera was never broken: a wedged USB device that opened cleanly and returned nothing. Unplug/replug fixed it. camera-doctor read mean 86.96 / max 255 / sd 58.54; camera-test then got 10 frames at 1280x720.

The map does not render because there is nothing to draw, not because unpkg failed. parse.py:265 fills status.positions ONLY from 'ongoingActivity { ... on OngoingWalk { positions } }' -- Fi returns position points only during a walk. A resting dog gives an empty list, and activity.html gates the container, stylesheet and script on '{% if map_points %}', so no map element renders at all.

SECURITY: app.py:170 keys the login lockout on request.client.host. Behind a Cloudflare tunnel that is 127.0.0.1 for every visitor, so all of the internet shares one bucket -- any stranger can lock out the household with five wrong guesses, and the per-attacker rate limit is gone entirely.

The session cookie sets httponly and samesite but not secure. Cannot be hard-coded True: that breaks LAN access over http:// because the browser silently stops sending the cookie and login never takes.
No security headers anywhere in app.py -- no CSP, X-Frame-Options, or Referrer-Policy.
views.py uses .astimezone(), which means the SERVER's timezone. Correct today, wrong the moment Chris is on the road -- which is the entire point of remote access.
queries.py:134-136 lists lastLocation and currentLocation as speculative, never confirmed. If lastLocation exists it is a much better answer for 'always show the map' than a static home pin.
decisions: Cloudflare Tunnel is the remote-access route: nothing inbound is opened, and a viewer needs no account (rules out port forwarding and Tailscale respectively).
The Secure-cookie fix needs a settings key, not a hard-coded True, so LAN access survives. Written up rather than done, because it needs tests for both states.
user-scalable=no is refused for pinch-to-zoom: iOS has ignored it since iOS 10 and it is a WCAG 1.4.4 failure. touch-action: manipulation on controls is the real fix.
A permanent map must never imply a live fix it does not have: walking = real track, not walking = home pin labelled as such, neither = say so like the camera says NO SIGNAL.
Pull-to-refresh should repaint from /activity.json, not location.reload(), so the MJPEG stream is not torn down.
lessons: A camera that opens and returns all-zero pixels is more likely a wedged USB device than hardware. The sd column separates them: 0.00 is wedged or blocked, a dark room has low mean but sd well above zero because a real sensor has read noise.
Check the repo before hedging. I marked the camera model 'unconfirmed' one commit after docs/next-session.md already recorded Chris confirming a C270 -- the evidence was one file away.

Diagnose in the code before repeating a standing assumption. Everyone including me assumed the missing map was the unpkg CDN; reading views.py and parse.py showed the template never renders a map element at all when map_points is empty.

Rate limits keyed on request.client.host silently become global buckets behind any reverse proxy or tunnel. Trust a forwarded-IP header only when explicitly configured -- an unconditionally trusted X-Forwarded-For is worse than none.
A security pass that lists only problems is dishonest about the code; recording what held up (constant-time compare, default-deny middleware, the avatar proxy's SVG exclusion) is part of the finding.

dont_retry: Do not blame the 1280x720 resolution request for black camera frames -- that was my hypothesis and camera-test disproved it by succeeding at exactly that size.
Do not assume the missing map is the unpkg CDN. That failure is real but produces a blank coloured box; an absent map element is the empty-map_points path instead.
Do not add user-scalable=no to the viewport meta. iOS ignores it and it breaks accessibility.
Do not hard-code secure=True on the session cookie -- it breaks LAN access and the login fails silently with no error.
Do not try to delete remote branches from this sandbox; the git proxy returns HTTP 403 on ref deletes.
